#### 5.10.18 Mighella (32 BBY)
- **Role:** Nightsister bodyguard to Garyn («Garyn's chief protector, Mighella, who is a Nightsister», L6175). Killed by Maul in the Black Sun massacre: «My blade halved the Nightsister after she tried to defeat me with summoned Force-lightning.» (L6397, Maul's report).
- **Scaling implications:** Maul > a lightning-using Nightsister, low difficulty (his own report).
- **Complete quote register (2 lines: every sentence that names Mighella, verbatim, in book order):**

  - Ch28 Chain of Command L6395 «"Not Mighella?"»

#### 5.10.21 Ni-Cada and Lo Bukk (~66 BBY)
- **Role:** a Cerean Jedi Master and his Zabrak Padawan on Abraxin («"I am Master Ni-Cada.» / «And this is Padawan Lo Bukk.», L2039), investigating the marsh-haunt killings. They track and kill Naat Lare while Plagueis watches without revealing himself.
- **Scaling implications:** they are the book's baseline Jedi. Plagueis avoids using the Force near them («should you call on the Force, you're likely to attract the Jedi», L2059, 11-4D).
- **Complete quote register (3 lines: every sentence that names Ni-Cada and Lo Bukk, verbatim, in book order):**
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L2039 «"I am Master Ni-Cada.»
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L2039 «And this is Padawan Lo Bukk.»
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L2045 «"And what brings the Jedi to Abraxin, Master Ni-Cada?»

#### 5.10.23 The Iktotchi prophetess of Saleucami (~66 BBY)
- **Role:** a precognitive Iktotchi who preaches transformation to a dark-side following (L1865–1891). She reads Plagueis at a touch: «You wear the darkness of the future. It is I who have sought you; I who should be your handmaiden.» (L1907). He kills her with trickled lightning (L1915).
- **Scaling implications:** P-67 kills a Force-strong seer in a crowd without being stopped. Plagueis kills her because her message «had doomed the Sith of old» (L1891).

- **Role:** Jedi archivist at the Serenno meeting. Her approach triggers Plagueis's dark-side reaction: «a feeling from deep in the dark side rose up inside him, strangling his» (L4321).

  - Ch17 Days of Wine and Impropriety L4299 «The silence that followed was broken by the voice of Jocasta Nu, who was summoning the Jedi to the far side of the conference room.»

  - Ch29 The Force Strikes Back L6895 «And so will support for Antilles, whose ambitions have blinded him to the fact that no one in the Senate wants an overzealous reformer in the chancellorship.»
  - Ch29 The Force Strikes Back L6947 «But for Yoda, Mace Windu, and the rest, Valorum is a known quantity, whereas Senators Antilles and Teem and you have yet to disclose your true agendas.»

  - Ch29 The Force Strikes Back L6845 «"Amedda can deny any request Valorum makes to convene the Senate in special session.»

#### 5.10.33 The Maladians (54 BBY)
- **Role:** the Jedi-killing assassin cult hired for the Vidar Kim hit and then for the Canted Circle ambush on Plagueis (Ch20). They cut his trachea but are «all but atomized» (see §3.1).
- **Key line:** Sidious afterwards: «for all the punishment his body had sustained at the hand» (L4865, of Plagueis).
- **Scaling implications:** P-54a survives an ambush by elite anti-Jedi assassins; the after-effect is P-54b.
- **Complete quote register (19 lines: every sentence that names The Maladians, verbatim, in book order):**
  - Ch16 Bold as Love L3933 «"The Maladians," Palpatine said.»
  - Ch16 Bold as Love L3941 «"Besides, the Maladians are known to honor all their contracts."»
  - Ch16 Bold as Love L4041 «In his apartment in snowbound Theed, Palpatine watched a HoloNet replay of Jedi Knight Ronhar Kim leaping from a Coruscant taxi in midflight onto a monospeeder piloted by the Maladian contracted to assassinate the elder Kim.»
  - Ch16 Bold as Love L4049 «"Is the Maladian alive?"»
  - Ch16 Bold as Love L4071 «"As I told you, the Maladians are very good at what they do."»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4703 «"The Maladian commander I did business with during the Kim affair."»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4707 «He said he'd just received word that a Maladian faction had accepted a contract to carry out a major hit on Coruscant, involving someone closely affiliated with Damask Holdings."»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4709 «Had the Santhe guards planned to turn him over to the Maladians following the holocommunication with Pax Teem?»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4721 «"As soon as I heard from the Maladian, I asked Kinman to keep an eye on them.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4755 «A few had lowered their black hoods, revealing themselves to be Maladians-the same group Sidious had employed to deal with Vidar Kim.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4757 «He wondered if the Maladians had actually been bold enough to kill the prominent Canted Circle members they were impersonating.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4761 «But the Maladians were far from run-of-the-mill murderers.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4765 «He stopped once to conjure a Force wave that all but atomized the bodies of six Maladians.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4767 «He was a moment from loosing hell on the Maladians when he sensed Sidious enter the room.»
  - Ch20 The Canted Circle L4787 «His fury notwithstanding, he would have preferred to linger until nightfall, which came early to that part of Coruscant, but he was certain that the Gran were expecting word that the Maladians had satisfied the terms of the contract, and he couldn't risk having them flee for the stars before he got to them.»
  - Ch21 Investiture L4817 «to enter the landmark building, let alone the order's vaunted initiation room, in which were discovered the bodies of two Echani, believed to be bodyguards; a dozen Muuns, killed by decapitator disks and vibroblades; and three times that number of Maladian assassins dressed in borrowed robes, who had succumbed to blaster bolts, blunt-force injuries, and, in some cases, traumatic»
  - Ch21 Investiture L4865 «Sidious had been wondering if Plagueis had been weakened by the attack, but he saw now that, for all the punishment his body had sustained at the hands of the Maladian assassins, the Muun was no less strong in the Force.»
  - Ch21 Investiture L4897 «"The Maladians..."»
  - Ch23 Under the Midnight Sun L5193 «If the Maladian attack had weakened him physically, it had also helped to shape his etheric body into a vessel sufficiently strong to contain the full power of the dark side.»

#### 5.10.36 Caar Damask (Plagueis's clan father; backstory)
- **Role:** administrator of Mygeeto (L1627), who gives the young Hego to Rugess Nome: «"You are of our blood, Hego, but we can no longer raise you as our progeny."» (L1645). Hego later learns the deal was made in fear of Nome (L1649).
- **Scaling implications:** none. Origin of Plagueis's Force potential and training under Tenebrous.
- **Complete quote register (11 lines: every sentence that names Caar Damask, verbatim, in book order):**
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1627 «So it happened that Plagueis's clan father, Caar Damask, came to be administrator of the treasure world of Mygeeto.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1631 «Success in supervising the mining operations came in short order, but contentment, of any sort, proved elusive until the arrival-ten years after his own-of a lower-caste Muun female who would first become his assistant, then his codicil wife, in due course giving birth to a son they named Hego, after Caar's clan father.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1633 «Even Caar found time enough from a demanding schedule to be a doting parent.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1641 «Worse, his father began to grow distant-even while Hego found himself becoming more and more a part of Caar's world.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1645 «Hego had made up his mind to bring his power to bear on the intolerable situation when, during one of Nome's visits, he was summoned to his father's office, where Caar, his mother, and the Bith were waiting.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1645 «Without looking at his wife, Caar had said, "You are of our blood, Hego, but we can no longer raise you as our progeny."»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1647 «Hego had looked from his father to his mother in mounting distress, fearing the very words Caar added a moment later.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1649 «A decade later, Hego would learn that while Caar had, in fact, done his best to keep his Force abilities to himself, he had come to the attention of Nome when the two had chanced to meet on High Port Space Center.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1649 «Years would pass before Nome found Hego's mother, whom he had conscripted not as an apprentice-for she wasn't strong enough in the Force-but as a disciple, whose task it had been to romance Caar and bear the fruit of that seduction: a child whom Nome and Bith science predicted would be born strong in the Force.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1649 «And then a deal had been brokered: Hego, in exchange for the realization of Caar Damask's lifelong dream of being accepted into the upper echelon of the InterGalactic Banking Clan.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1651 «Five years after the revelation in the office, Caar was recalled to Muunilinst to become director of the treasury branch of the IBC.»

#### 5.10.37 Darth Bane (lore)
- **Role:** the Sith'ari of legend, founder of the Rule of Two. «In the thousand years since his death, Bane had become deified; the powers attributed to him, legendary.» (L191). Plagueis's view: Bane «hadn't been able to harness those energies» of sorcery as well as others (L1227).
- **Scaling implications:** lore statement only.
- **Complete quote register (37 lines: every sentence that names Darth Bane, verbatim, in book order):**
  - Ch1 The Underworld L177 «"Darth Bane would appreciate our efforts," the Sith Master was telling his apprentice as they stood side by side in the crystalline cave that had drawn them across the stars.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L181 «"Darth Bane's early years," Plagueis said through his transpirator mask.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L185 «"Bane's seminal years," he corrected.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L191 «The aptly named Darth Bane, who had redefined the Sith by limiting their number and operating from concealment, had mined cortosis as a youth on Apatros long before embracing the tenets of the dark side.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L191 «In the thousand years since his death, Bane had become deified; the powers attributed to him, legendary.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L337 «As Darth Bane would have wished, Plagueis thought.»
  - Ch1 The Underworld L389 «In Bane's age a Sith might have had to guard against an attempt at essence transfer by the deceased-a leap into the consciousness of the Sith who survived-but those times were long past and of no relevance; not since the teachings had been sabotaged, the technique lost.»
  - Ch2 The Inner Landscape L439 «He knew from his travels with and without Tenebrous that he wasn't the galaxy's sole practitioner of the dark side-nor Sith for that matter, since the galaxy was rife with pretenders-but he was now the only Sith Lord descended from the Bane line.»
  - Ch2 The Inner Landscape L443 «He had read the legends of Bane; how he had been hounded by the lingering presences of those he had defeated in order to rid the Sith Order of infighting, and return the Order to a genuine hegemony by instating the Rule of Two: a Master to embody power; an apprentice to crave it.»
  - Ch2 The Inner Landscape L443 «To hear it told, Bane had even been hounded by the spirits of generations-dead Sith Lords whose tombs and manses he had desecrated in his fervent search for holocrons and other ancient devices offering wisdom and guidance.»
  - Ch5 Homecoming L1227 «Darth Bane had referred to sorcery as one of the purest expressions of the dark side of the Force, and yet he hadn't been able to harness those energies with near the skill as had his onetime apprentice Zannah.»
  - Ch5 Homecoming L1227 «Bane's disciples, however, believed that he had experimented with a technique of even greater significance: that of essence transfer, which he had learned after acquiring and plundering the holocron of Darth Andeddu, and which involved the relocation of an individual's consciousness into another body or, in some cases, a talisman, temple, or sarcophagus.»
  - Ch5 Homecoming L1231 «Nor did he seek to shunt his mind into the body of another, whether an apprentice, as Bane was thought to have attempted, or some vat-grown clone.»
  - Ch5 Homecoming L1239 «The task before him was at once invigorating and daunting, and in the eye of that cycloning storm he could hear the faraway voices of all those who had laid the goundwork of the Sith imperative-the Grand Plan; those who had enlivened the hurricane with their breath and lives: Darths Bane and Zannah, and on down through the generations that had included Cognus, Vectivus, Ramage, and Tenebrous.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1595 «The young Bith would have done well in Bane's era.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1605 «Like Plagueis, Tenebrous had obviously embraced the fact that Darth Bane's Rule of Two had expired.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1605 «But while most Sith Lords since Bane had in their own fashion helped to weaken the Republic, their efforts had owed less to selflessness and allegiance to the Rule than to weakness and incompetence.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1605 «Driven to discharge Bane's imperative they might have been, and yet each had fallen prey to individual foibles and eccentricities, and so had failed to exact revenge on the the Jedi Order.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1619 «For the past five hundred years, the Sith of the Bane line had eschewed selecting children as apprentices, finding it more advantageous to discover beings who had already been hardened or scarred by life.»
  - Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand L1657 «As Tenebrous explained it, the Jedi had emerged strong from the war of a millennium earlier, and while Darth Bane and subsequent Sith Lords had done their best to disrupt the reborn Republic, they labored at a disadvantage.»
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L1769 «A powerful female Shi'ido named Belia Darzu had been a Sith Lord in the pre-Bane era, creating armies of technobeasts she controlled using dark side energy.»
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L1891 «While the notion of having a ready-made army of dark siders available to him was not without a certain appeal, the Iktotchi was spreading a message that had doomed the Sith of old, the Sith who preceded Bane's reformation, and had allowed internecine fighting to propel the Order into oblivion.»
  - Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device L2009 «Abraxin had been strong in the dark side during Bane's lifetime, when it had been aligned with Lord Kaan's Brotherhood of Darkness, but Plagueis could sense that the power had waned significantly in the intervening centuries.»
  - Ch12 Seduced by the Dark Side of the Force L3145 «Then, Sidious, we must do our best to sabotage the dynamic Darth Bane set in motion, because we will need each other if we're to realize our ultimate goals.»
  - Ch13 Riders on the Storm L3245 «"Darth Bane advised: One day the Republic will fall and the Jedi will be wiped out.»

## 6. Scaling connections and quick ladder (this book only)

**Direct on-page results:**
- P-67 > T-67 (surprise kill; in raw speed T-67 > P-67).
- P-67 > V-67 (duel, mid diff).
- P-65 ≫ S-64 (training).
- P-54a > S-54 (surprise choke; concealment from S-54).
- S-33 > M-33 (Hypori test, disarm).
- S-32 > P-32 *(drunk, asleep, not defending; an ambush, not a duel)*.
- M-32 > Mighella, Garyn (who wounded him), Sinya, and two Jedi (reported).
- Ni-Cada > Naat Lare.
- Maul (TPM) > Qui-Gon (TPM) and < Obi-Wan (Padawan), per the Epilogue report.

**Quick ladder (book-internal, by version):**
1. **S-32+** (post-boost; «Had the Force ever been so strong in anyone?») ≥ **P-33/32** (prime; «nuclear oval»; Sidious POV unsure whether he is «a level behind») ≈ **S-33/32**. The book leaves the P-32 vs S-32 order deliberately open, with the internal POV leaning Plagueis.
2. P-41 (amp) > P-54b ≈ P-54a > P-65 > P-67. Each step is a real power gain, but the count rose only at P-41.
3. S-54 (a «true Sith Lord», «more than equal to the most powerful of the Jedi» as a pair) > S-64 > S-65 (untrained, but bulkhead-buckling).
4. Qui-Gon (QG-32) ≈ Dooku (D-33) > Maul (M-33)? The book only rates them; it shows no fights. In Sidious's framing Qui-Gon is a «master sword fighter» above Obi-Wan.
5. T-67 ≈ P-67 in raw power (unknown); V-67 < P-67.
6. Maul (M-32) > Mighella, Garyn, Pavan (who outwits him).

## 7. Verdict implications (matchups this book informs)

Scale: low diff ≈ 8.5/10+ win rate, mid ≈ 6.5–8, high ≈ 5.5–6 (house mapping from verdicts.md).

### 7.1 Plagueis (prime, P-33/32) vs Sidious (TPM, S-33/32, pre-boost): **Plagueis, high diff (~6/10)**. CONFIRMS the current "slight Plagueis lean vs TPM Sidious"
- **For Plagueis:**
  - At S-33, Sidious is privately unsure he has caught up: «Was he a level behind? Two levels behind?» L5255.
  - He «couldn't be certain he had learned all of Plagueis's secrets» L5255, including «the ability to prevent beings from dying» (same line).
  - The P-41 amp is on the page: «increased midi-chlorian count» L5445.
  - P-32 can kill by midi-chlorian command L6355 («I am killing you»).
  - His precognition is far better than S-32's (§3.1 #46 vs §3.2 #24).
  - Even dying and choked, he raised a Force storm that (L7243 «A Force storm gathered over the couch») that hurled objects around Sidious.
  - The doctrine Sidious quotes says outright that the apprentice need not be **stronger**, only «more clever» L7247.
- **For Sidious:**
  - He won, and the only time the two "fought", Plagueis's power did not save him.
  - He claims parity («his equally powerful apprentice» L7237) and the resurrection skill L7237.
  - He shrugged through the Force storm.
  - P-54a choked S-54 only by surprise, and S-54 «pledged also never again to lower his guard» L3827.
- **Why high diff, not mid:** the book gives no fair-fight data, and Sidious's lightning-plus-choke was enough once Plagueis declined to defend. A fight rule that lets midi-chlorian killing work at combat speed would push it to mid diff Plagueis. Ruling it too slow (the Veruna kill took a whole conversation) keeps it at high diff.

### 7.2 Plagueis (prime) vs Sidious (ROTS → DE peak): **Sidious, high diff (~6/10)**. CONFIRMS (medium-low)
- This book pins the S-32+ boost: «less a transformation than an intensification-a gravitic shift» L117.
- Every post-TPM Sidious is a separate, higher version. The Plagueis book supplies the amp, and the other sources (ROTS, Dark Empire) supply the growth.
- Nothing in this book argues that P-32 would match a post-boost, post-ROTS Sidious.

### 7.3 Plagueis (prime) vs Mace Windu (ROTS, Vaapad): **Plagueis, mid-high diff (~6/10)**. CONFIRMS the result, but the reasoning needs a fix
- **For Plagueis:**
  - He was rated a dueling «master of the art» L1547 (P-67).
  - He beat a style-counter specialist with the «marionette» trick L1553.
  - Bolt absorption L835 («absorbed the bolts»).
  - The atomizing Force wave L4765 («all but atomized»).
  - Shield, sonic roar, choke, and the P-41+ amp.
- **Against Plagueis:**
  - He hates dueling («tedious affairs» L1547).
  - His lightning failed under heart strain.
  - Battle meditation, shatterpoint and Vaapad have nothing comparable in this book.
  - The midi-chlorian kill needs time.
- **Fix:** verdicts.md says Plagueis survived "and shrugging off" Sidious's lightning. The text has the lightning **ground on his breathing device**. He «stopped short of defending himself», then suffocated and was choked to death. That is **"survived two lightning barrages without defending, then died of suffocation and choke"**, not "shrugged off". Use it as a durability data point only.

### 7.4 Sidious (any era) vs Mace: **Sidious ~7/10 (mid)**. CONFIRMS
- The only new datum is S-54's self-assessment: the pair is «more than equal to the most powerful of the Jedi Order» L4339.

### 7.5 Plagueis (prime) vs Yoda (ROTS): **toss-up, slight Plagueis lean (~5.5/10, high diff, low confidence)**. NEW proposal; verdicts.md lists it as "NOT judged"
- The book's statements for the pair at 54 BBY put them above any single Jedi (C12).
- P-54a hides from four Jedi at conversation range, including two Masters.
- Plagueis shows precognition and life/death control that Yoda doesn't.
- Against him: none of this is Yoda-specific; Yoda appears only as «troubled» L2455; and the general "the Jedi are blind" framing comes from the dark side's clouding, not from raw power. **Low confidence; the book alone can't settle it.**

### 7.6 Plagueis vs Krayt (reborn): **no new data**. Keep the slight Plagueis lean
- The book adds the P-41 amp and the resurrection feat, both already counted in verdicts.md ("life/death mastery").

### 7.7 Dooku vs Maul (TPM): **Dooku ~6.5/10 (mid)**. CONFIRMS and slightly strengthens
- Already in verdicts: «he fought well, even after I deprived him of his lightsaber» L5205 (S-33 > M-33).
- New in this read:
  - Plagueis: «you allowed him to believe that he is more skilled than he actually is» L5215.
  - Maul is wounded by a lightly Force-sensitive Garyn L6441 («cut open your hand»).
  - Pavan outwits him L6441.
  - Dooku is rated «one of the Order's finest lightsaber masters» L4185 (D-54) and «most skilled duelists» L5723 (D-33).

### 7.8 Maul (TPM) vs Obi-Wan (TPM, Padawan) / Qui-Gon (TPM)
- **Framing:** «a master sword fighter only to be overcome by a lesser one» L7317 (Sidious POV).
- So Maul > Qui-Gon (on-page TPM), and Obi-Wan's win is framed as an upset. Maul vs Obi-Wan (TPM) leans **Maul ~6/10** in a rematch, by this book's framing. Low weight: it's a single POV line.

### 7.9 Sidious vs Dooku: **Sidious, low diff, high confidence**. CONFIRMS
- «Dooku had talent, and could be a powerful placeholder.» L7477
- Plagueis: Dooku «would never be content to serve as an apprentice» (Ch26), a political risk rather than a power threat.

### 7.10 Dooku vs Obi-Wan/Anakin, Grievous vs the Jedi: **not informed by this book**
- Grievous doesn't appear.
- Anakin appears only at age 9, and Obi-Wan only as a Padawan or new Knight. See the Labyrinth of Evil notes (another worker).

### 7.11 Where Plagueis ranks among the Sith ("top 3")
- **The book CONFIRMS Plagueis at #3 among the Sith** (after Vitiate and Sidious in the current tiers; he sits in tier 4 with Yoda and Krayt).
- Why the book doesn't support moving him above Sidious:
  - Sidious beats him on the page, by ambush.
  - Sidious's post-boost and later growth are separate versions.
  - The best Plagueis evidence is utility/sorcery-adjacent (resurrection, midi-chlorian kills), not mass-scale destruction.
- Why it doesn't support moving him below Krayt: no Krayt data here, and the P-41 amp plus the life/death feats are unique.

## 8. Story and prose notes (SP1–SP6)
- **SP1, the thesis is cleverness over strength.** The doctrine «An apprentice no longer needs to be stronger... merely more clever» L7247 is turned against its author. Luceno sets up the Rule of Two's return without settling who was stronger. This ambiguity is deliberate, and it explains why Luceno himself later hedged ("If it had come to a duel, I think Plagueis may have found a way to undermine his apprentice", Del Rey Facebook Q&A, Jan 25 2012; external, not from the book).
- **SP2, the Force as an agent.** The dark side chokes Plagueis's voice (Ch17), «whispered» the murder to Sidious L7213 («and the dark side whispered»), and Plagueis treats Sojourn's destruction as «the work of the Force» L6119. The book's metaphysics, that the Force «will strike back» L4895, frames Anakin as the Force's counterstroke (Ch29 title). For scaling, this means some outcomes are narrative destiny rather than power.
- **SP3, POV and unreliability.** Sidious's internal POVs (C5, C6) are more trustworthy than his gloating speech (C7–C10). Plagueis's self-assessments («no powers beyond his reach») are contradicted by the narration («never succeeded in duplicating any of those phenomena»).
- **SP4, the tie-in web.** Woven in:
  - *Cloak of Deception* (Eriadu, Havac, Valorum's aurodium).
  - *Saboteur* (Dorvalla).
  - *Shadow Hunter* (Monchar, Pavan, the two Jedi).
  - *Maul: Lockdown* (Komari Vosa).
  - *Labyrinth of Evil* (Sifo-Dyas, the clone order, Dooku's departure).
  - *Dark Lord* (11-4D's new body).
  - TCW (Dathomir, «Half a clan pair»).
  - KOTOR/Old Republic lore (Malak, Revan, Vitiate, Ommin, Sion, Nihilus).
- **SP5, structure.** It is a three-generation story with 20-year jumps. Each part ends on a power transition: Tenebrous's death leads to Sidious's naming; the Maladian ambush to the transpirator; Plagueis's death to Sidious alone. The Prologue starts at the end of Ch30.
- **SP6, prose.** Dense with political names, financial jargon and Expanded Universe lore. Combat is rare and short; Ch4, Ch6, Ch20 and Ch30 are the four real action set pieces. A lot of the "feats" are dropped into exposition (resurrection, the shift), so they are **narrated feats** with no combat test.

## 9. Biggest scaling takeaways (Darth Plagueis)
1. **Plagueis has three real amp steps, all on the page.**
   - The Rule-of-Two succession at 67 BBY: «recent amplification of his powers», but the count is flat.
   - The Maladian crucible at 54 BBY, which forged «a vessel sufficiently strong to contain the full power of the dark side».
   - The P-41 shift and resurrection, after which his midi-chlorian count «increased».
   - So P-33/32 is his prime, and P-67 is a much weaker version.
2. **The "fight" with Sidious was an ambush.** Plagueis was drunk and asleep after twenty sleepless years, and he «stopped short of defending himself». He absorbed two lightning barrages through his breathing mask, raised a Force storm while suffocating, and died of choke and asphyxia. Don't scale it as a fair fight in either direction, and don't call it "shrugging off" lightning.
3. **Sidious at TPM is privately unsure he has caught Plagueis** («a level behind? Two levels behind?»). His «tenfold» growth is his own estimate, and his claim of parity («equally powerful») comes from a gloating speech. Weight: a slight Plagueis edge over TPM Sidious; Sidious wins after the boost.
4. **Midi-chlorian feats are real but not combat-tested.**
   - Resurrection: Venamis, repeatedly, while comatose.
   - Self-rejuvenation.
   - Force-induced pregnancies.
   - Killing by command: Veruna, over a conversation.
   - Self-rescue failed under suffocation.
   - Treat these as utility and hax with unknown combat speed.
5. **Raw power peak:** P-54b, mortally wounded, «all but atomized the bodies of six Maladians» and swept the wave through six more. Add bare-hand bolt absorption into lightning at P-67, and a dueling «master of the art» rating.
6. **Sidious version anchors:** at S-65 an untrained teen buckles a starship bulkhead. At S-54 he is a blur-speed solo massacre machine who teaches himself sorcery. At S-33 he disarms Maul (this overrides the DSSB "nearly bested"). S-32+ is the Prologue's «intensification» boost.
7. **Precognition favors Plagueis** (the cyborg vision, Naboo's loss, Maul's end) over TPM Sidious («none came»; «sensed nothing» about Anakin). This tilts any prep-time scenario toward Plagueis.
8. **The book's thesis is cleverness over strength**, so its outcome (Sidious wins) is not evidence that Sidious is stronger.

## 11. Quote verification report

- **Script:** `[local path]`, modeled on `verify_kotor_quotes.py`.
  - Normalization: curly quotes become straight; all double-quote marks are removed (so quotes that span a dialogue tag still match); whitespace is collapsed.
  - Matching: each «…» quote is split on `...`/`…` into fragments; fragments under 4 characters are ignored; each fragment must be an exact substring of the normalized book text.
  - Line check: when an `L####` cite directly follows a quote, the fragment must also appear within ±3 lines of that cite.
- **Run on this file (2026-10-19, America/New_York):** **1,452 «…» quotes → 1,502 fragments checked, 0 failures, 0 line-cite offsets.** (This includes the body, Appendix A and the Appendix B log; Appendix A repeats the register.)
- **Re-run after the 2026-10-19 gap fix (America/New_York):** **2,924 «…» quotes → 2,976 fragments checked, 0 failures, 0 line-cite offsets** for the whole file. New material:
  - §5.9–5.10 now hold 43 individual profiles (previously two grouped lists), each with a complete auto-harvested register of every sentence that names the character. That adds 1,239 register lines, plus the profile prose quotes.
  - Appendix A.0 adds 140 hand-curated pronoun-only and epithet-only lines: Plagueis 69, Sidious 31, Maul 18, Venamis 4, Sifo-Dyas 3, Ronhar Kim 3, Tenebrous 2, Dooku 2, Anakin 2, Qui-Gon 1, Vidar Kim 1, Nute Gunray 1, the Iktotchi prophetess 1, Mighella 1, Alexi Garyn 1.
- **Quote register** (`quotes-plag.txt`, the source for Appendix A): **748 entries → 750 fragments, 0 failures, 0 line-cite offsets.** Unique register quotes per character: Plagueis 319, Sidious 186, Maul 58, Dooku 40, Tenebrous 29, Anakin 27, Venamis 19, Padmé 18, Qui-Gon 16, Sifo-Dyas 13, Obi-Wan 10, Yoda 9, Mace 4.
- **Failures found and fixed while writing:**
  - 5 in the reading log. Capitalization: "Half a clan pair", "the Force tells me"; dropped diacritics: "ter?s k?si"; my own bracket edits: "hurl[s]", and "To extend" where the text has "The goal is to extend".
  - 4 in the body: two paraphrases put in guillemets (fixed), and two verdicts.md phrases that aren't book text (moved to straight quotes).
  - 1 mis-attached line cite (fixed).
- **Not book text** (deliberately outside guillemets): the Luceno Facebook Q&A line, and verdicts.md wording.
- **Caveat:** the Appendix B reading log cites chapter-start lines for some quotes. Those are reported as line-cite offsets (if any), not failures; the text itself matches.

## Appendix B. Raw reading log (written chunk by chunk while reading)


### Prologue (L111–167) — Sidious at Plagueis's death [32 BBY, after TPM]
- Plot: Tremor "sprung from death"; Sidious stands at window of the suite, Plagueis dead on floor; room disarrayed "as if a whirlwind"; Sidious fears Plagueis may have faked death; rolls body over with the Force; confirms death; exults; the dark side "anoint[s]" him. Wonders how Tenebrous died.
- FEAT/STATE Sidious (32 BBY, at Plagueis's death = post-boost begins): L117 «the Force so strong within him that he feared he might disappear into it»; «less a transformation than an intensification-a gravitic shift». L163 «Had the Force ever been so strong in anyone?» (POV rhetorical). L159 «The dark side had made him its property, and now he made the dark side his.»
- Sidious uncertain about Plagueis immortality: L133 «Had Plagueis unlocked the key to immortality, and survived after all?»; L145 «though he could save others from death-he had failed to save himself.» (Plagueis could save others from death = feat statement for Plagueis 32 BBY)
- Sidious caution: L131, L137 «Wary of approaching the corpse of his former Master, he called on the Force to roll the aged Muun over» — implies fear of Plagueis even dead.

### Ch1 The Underworld (L171–389) — Bal'demnic, 67 BBY; Tenebrous murdered
- Plot: Tenebrous (Bith) & Plagueis (Muun) in cortosis cave on Bal'demnic. Mining probe (from Subtext Mining—later revealed Tenebrous's secret apprentice Venamis? actually Tenebrous's maxi-chlorian scheme; note) refuses orders and drills into lethane. Both Sith fire lightning into the shaft; cortosis resists. Flight; explosion. Tenebrous Force-shields the fireball; both hold up the ceiling; Plagueis drops slabs on Tenebrous, breaks his neck, observes his midi-chlorians die.
- FEATS: Tenebrous + Plagueis lightning into shaft (L267) blocked by ore «There's too much resistance here» (L271). Plagueis «had to call deeply on the Force merely to keep up» with Tenebrous's run (L293) — Tenebrous speed > Plagueis 67 BBY. Tenebrous Force shield contains fireball (L305) «conjured a Force shield with his waving arms that met the fireball and contained it». Both hold slabs (L309–311). Plagueis brings slabs down «so quickly and with so much momentum that Tenebrous was buried almost before he understood» (L321). Breaks neck (L375). Perceives midi-chlorians but cannot manipulate yet (L377).
- Precognition: Tenebrous foresaw danger (death at Plagueis's hand) but misread it (L317–323).

### Ch2 The Inner Landscape (L393–471) — Plagueis alone on Bal'demnic
- Plot: Plagueis wounded (back pulped), numbs pain; levitates slabs to make a ramp; Force-blows the canopy; takes both lightsabers, erases navicomputer; leaps out; runs at blur speed to spaceport over two nights; senses «near-equal power» (Venamis/the other—foreshadow of Tenebrous's maxi-chlorian/ Venamis, and/or Palpatine); vision of Bal'demnic in the Clone Wars; slices spaceport and picks the freighter Woebegone (Capt. Ellin Lah).
- FEATS Plagueis 67 BBY: self-healing/pain numbing (L399); TK slabs (L409); Force blows through transparisteel (L411); blur speed (L427); body-temperature control (L429); precog of Clone Wars (L461); can't Force-leap through a high oculus unaided (L405) — limit.

### Ch3 Woebegone (L475–811) — stowaway, 67 BBY
- Plot: Woebegone crew introduced (Capt. Ellin Lah, Togruta; first mate Maa Kaap, Zabrak; pilot Blir', Balosar; navigator Semasalli, Dresselian; Wandau, Klatooinian; PePe Rossh, Kaleesh; Doo Zuto, Quara; droid 11-4D). Plagueis found in a frozen cargo container; survives cold via two voluntary hearts. Offers payment; crew debates ransom; decides to comm Bal'demnic. Plagueis: «I can't permit this, Captain» — fates "sealed" by the Force.
- FEATS: survive freezer via voluntary cardiac control (L617); precog/fatalism (L807 «Their fates had been sealed from the instant Plagueis had glimpsed the ship»).

### Ch4 The Meaning of Death (L815–1011) — Woebegone massacre (Plagueis ~67 BBY, wounded)
- Plot (11-4D POV): Plagueis kills Lah off-page (near-decapitation), then the crew: deflects/returns all bolts with saber + bare hand; throws saber to kill Blir' and maim Semasalli; ABSORBS blaster bolts with bare hand and re-emits as lightning on Wandau; kicks Maa Kaap across the cabin (spine snap); grabbed by Zuto/PePe, «as if the Muun had turned to stone»; spins blade, kills PePe, maims Zuto. Tries to heal/prolong survivors: Maa Kaap revived briefly then dies; fails because he can't yet engage midi-chlorians. Kills Wandau with finger click. Goes to Deep Space Demo and Removal station (Boss Cabra / Black Sun-adjacent; Nikto female, Dug Darnada); is "Magister Damask"; orders ship slagged; keeps 11-4D.
- KEY FEATS (Plagueis ~67 BBY, injured, fatigued): L831 evade/deflect/return every shot; L835 absorbs bolts → lightning («stretched out his right hand and absorbed the bolts... fountain from the hand... as a tangle of blue electricity»); L839 kick kills Zabrak; L841 immovable «as if the Muun had turned to stone»; L845 Force-healing revives Maa Kaap temporarily; L879 healing of tissue is «no more difficult than levitating slabs of stone» but midi-chlorians not yet responsive; L881 Lah's reflexes nearly let her dodge; «sloppiness on his part, owing to fatigue and blood loss».
- L883 senses midi-chlorians directly, beyond blood tests; ancient Sith drew on death energies — lost knowledge.

### Ch5 Homecoming (L1015–1239) — Muunilinst, 67 BBY
- Plot: Hego Damask returns to High Port; Larsh Hill (Damask Holdings) meets him; rival Chairman Tonith (IBC) needles him about free-trade zones lobbied by the Jedi; Trade Federation gains full Senate voting. Damask reveals "Rugess Nome" (Tenebrous's cover identity, starship designer) is dead; orders Bal'demnic mining rights bought; invites Subtext Mining to the Gathering. Aborah (Damask clan smoker island): library of Sith lore (Rakata, Dai Bendu, Malreaux, Sorcerers of Tund, ysalimiri, taozin) and labs (vivisection, hybridization). Goal: «extend my life indefinitely. To conquer death.» His midi-chlorian count did not rise despite power amplification. Theory of midi-chlorians: compliant in the weak-willed; induce them to create new cells. Ancient sorcery lore (Naga Sadow, Exar Kun, Zannah, Andeddu, essence transfer). He rejects disembodied survival: wants corporeal immortality. Feels dark side as a hurricane; lineage Bane→Zannah→Cognus→Vectivus→Ramage→...→Tenebrous's Twi'lek Master (Darth Gravid lost knowledge).
- STATE: L1221 «Despite the recent amplification of his powers he sensed that his midi-chlorian count had not increased since the events on Bal'demnic» — Rule-of-Two succession boost for Plagueis 67 BBY. L1237 «as a hurricane».

### Ch6 The Hunters' Moon (L1243–1575) — Gathering on Sojourn; DUEL Plagueis vs Venamis (67 BBY)
- Plot: Sojourn moon (Echani Sun Guards, greel forests, cloned game). Damask meetings: Gardulla Besadii (backs her Tatooine grab + Boonta Podrace; wants Boss Cabra on Nar Shaddaa, Black Sun/Alexi Garyn); Yinchorri Qayhuk — RESISTANT to Force suggestion (L1333); demands a "personal favor"; Senator Pax Teem (Gran) storms out (to be shown expendable); Subtext Mining Gossams put on laser-cannon platform; they reveal Naboo plasma reservoir; exiled to Tingel Arm. Steering committee (Narro Sienar, Canted Circle, TF directorate; "tactical astriction", oligarchy goal). Perimeter breach: Plagueis senses a Force-user, minimizes his presence, meets a Bith with red saber: Darth Venamis, Tenebrous's secret second apprentice. Duel. Venamis yields; Plagueis forces him to eat a poison blossom «But I will make certain you don't die.»
- DUEL FEATS (L1547–1559): Tenebrous «had pronounced Plagueis a master of the art»; Venamis hangs suspended in air after Plagueis Force-blows his branch; Venamis trained in Plagueis's style, counters every move, sears Plagueis's neck; Plagueis «took himself out of his body and began working his material self like a marionette»; then «came back into himself with such fury that his lightsaber became a blinding rod»; scorches Venamis chest to chin, disarms, Force-pulls Venamis's saber faster than Venamis; senses lightning building; «Yield!». Implication: Plagueis 67 BBY is a master duelist (by Tenebrous) who dislikes saber duels; won versus a specialist counter-stylist, mid diff, took a hit.
- Force suggestion fails on Yinchorri (L1333) — limit; Plagueis can mask his presence (L1493 «minimized his presence in the Force, surrendering his eminence»).

### Ch7 There Where They Used to Stand (L1579–1661) — Venamis in bacta; Plagueis backstory
- Plot: Venamis kept comatose in bacta at Aborah as experimental subject (high midi-chlorian count; «great potential in the Force and yet still be inept»). Venamis had been scouting apprentices. Tenebrous–Plagueis ideological split: Tenebrous = Bith science/future-casting fatalism; Plagueis = not a fatalist, eliminate competitors. Rule of Two «had expired» in both their views. Backstory: Hego born on Mygeeto to Caar Damask and a lower-caste Muun mother who was Tenebrous's disciple, bred via Bith science to be strong in the Force; at <5 years he Force-compels a playmate to jump out a window; traded to Rugess Nome (Tenebrous) for Caar's IBC promotion. Tenebrous's teachings: «A phantom menace... revenge... by contagion». Tenebrous's compliment: «You are such a one.»

### Ch8 Victims of Their Own Device (L1665–2113) — hunting Venamis's candidates (67–65 BBY)

Leverage to install Narro Sienar. (b) Saleucami: Iktotchi prophetess with proven precognition prophesies Clone Wars, Empire, despot; she senses «You wear the darkness of the future»; Plagueis kills her by trickling lightning through her hands; mind-tricks Twi'lek disciple. (c) Bedlam asylum: Nautolan Naat Lare escaped with "a Bith physician" (Venamis); Abraxin marsh-haunt killings; Jedi Master Ni-Cada (Cerean) and Padawan Lo Bukk (Zabrak) investigating; Plagueis hides presence («anchored himself in the material realm»), calls Naat Lare with the Force from underwater, orders him to kill the Jedi; Naat Lare is killed by Ni-Cada (one Jedi injured).

Plagueis wants «a partner rather than an underling» — Sith line continues through him. Plagueis can glean little from Palpatine via the Force.

I was death itself!» Walls down: «the Force was powerful in him!» Plagueis menaces: «What you sense is a fraction of what I can bring to bear.» Palpatine kneels → named Sidious.

Precognition as a youth (L2701). Concealment since infancy (L3055 «the walls he had raised perhaps since infancy»). Infant strength (L2905).

- Plot: Plagueis (snow melts before touching him, minimal clothing) trains Sidious in frozen deprivation; makes him retell the murders; teaches: Sith «stalk the Force like hunters»; envy dynamic must be sabotaged — «until I've guided you to parity... we will need each other». Scree-slope trial: Sidious lunges at a Force illusion of Plagueis; repelled «irresistible force»; TK-lifted without touching; lightsaber burns; «Not a standard day sooner than a decade.»

Venamis still alive/comatose. Theory: Jedi light-side "bubble"; Celestials as midi-chlorian supervisors; greater Sith goal = «toppling the Force itself»; Vitiate mention; Plagueis «Already he could command them to promote healing». ### Ch28 Chain of Command (L6377–6785): Maul's Black Sun massacre, clone order via Sifo-Dyas, Pavan, the blockade (~32 BBY)
- Plot: Maul killed Sinya by decapitation and halved Mighella «after she tried to defeat me with summoned Force-lightning». He drowned Garyn, but Garyn (slightly Force-sensitive) cut his hand first. Maul revealed to Garyn that he answers to a Master and spoke of «revenge of the Sith». Sidious: «When you face someone strong in the Force you must remain focused... deliver a killing strike». Maul is exiled to Orsis to train. Sidious wonders whether he himself would gloat, and whether Plagueis revealed himself to Veruna; «the dark side's growing impatience, and its demand for full disclosure». In Monument Plaza, Damask on Maul: «Again, the Zabrak proves his value». Black Sun now goes to Xixor and Sise Fromm. Panaka and the handmaidens. War plan: Baktoid to Geonosis, a long war, a «grown army», a surprise attack at the end of the war (Order 66 seed); the Kaminoans said humans would be «easier to replicate». The Monchar holocron problem (Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter): Damask's eyes «flashed yellow»; «Palpatine took comfort in the fact that even Plagueis had his limits.» Perlemian Orbital Facility: Maul has killed two Jedi and a Hutt in the Crimson Corridor. Damask: Maul «has the skill to scramble the minds of ordinary beings, but not to cloak himself from a Jedi» (L6563). Present: Jorus C'baoth, Yoda, Mace Windu, Adi Gallia, Bail Antilles, Teem. DAMASK RECRUITS SIFO-DYAS: he predicts civil war within «fifteen years at the most» and proposes «a human army a million strong... in as few as ten years», with a down payment through untraceable accounts. Sifo-Dyas: «You have read my thoughts, Magister. I have also sensed that war is imminent». Lorn Pavan handed the holocron to Palpatine; his hand had been cut off by Maul, and Maul later kills him («Cost cutting»). Damask: «the Force tells me that he will do it... We have become invincible.» Valorum's graphs uncover the arms buildup. Amidala's holo reports the blockade.
### Ch29 The Force Strikes Back (L6789–7049): TPM events, Plagueis's precognition, discovery of Anakin ★
- Plot: The blockade underwhelms. Damask lobbies for a co-chancellorship. Valorum sends Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan. Plagueis: «I have met Qui-Gon, and he is nothing like some of the others Dooku trained.»; «Qui-Gon will evade detection by the droids and wreak slow but inevitable havoc on the flagship.» Sidious: «Two lone Jedi are no match for thousands of battle droids». The invasion moves up. Plagueis watches Sidious and Maul on a balcony «his presence in the Force minimized». 11-4D lip-reads: «At last we reveal ourselves to the Jedi»; «You have been well trained, my young apprentice. They will be no match for you.» PLAGUEIS PRECOGNITION: «the gates that obscured the future parted and he had a glimpse of events to come, or events that might come. Either way, he was not encouraged.» He foresees that this is the last meeting of Sidious and Maul in the flesh (L6875). Maul's Tatooine skirmish with Qui-Gon. Teem is smeared with Jabba's help; the Antilles reformer is undercut. Plagueis stays away from the Queen's landing so the Jedi won't sense «our leanings». The no-confidence vote is engineered through Amidala. At Mok's Cheap Eats, Dooku tells Palpatine about Anakin, «Perhaps conceived by the Force»: midi-chlorian count «unprecedented», the vergence, the Boonta win, and that Qui-Gon «dueled with an assassin who is well trained in the Jedi arts... a Sith». Dooku: «We all think that there's much more to you than meets the eye». Palpatine: «And I sensed nothing about him.» (Anakin slept in Palpatine's suite.) Plagueis rushes to 500 Republica and Force-compels a handmaiden («You have my permission to speak»), but Qui-Gon has already taken Anakin to the Temple. «Are we undone? ... Have you undone us?»
- FEATS/limits: Plagueis precognition (L6869–6875), Force-suppression of his presence (L6853), mind compulsion (L7027). Sidious fails to sense Anakin (L6995). Maul vs Garyn (L6397–6441), mind-scramble but no cloaking (L6563).
### Ch30 Taking the Future from the Now (L7053–7301): Palpatine nominated; Plagueis's last vision; THE MURDER ★★
- Plot: Damask is still unnerved, has missed Anakin. «High midi-chlorian counts don't always equate to Force talents. You told me yourself.» / «That's not what concerns me.» Orn Free Taa nominates Palpatine: «You've done it, Darth Plagueis» / «Not yet... I will not rest until I'm certain of a win.»
- On the observatory, Plagueis watches Qui-Gon and Anakin through macrobinoculars and reaches out with the Force: «ferocious battles in deep space; the clashing of lightsabers; partitions of radiant light; a black-helmeted cyborg rising from a table...» «The boy would change the course of history... Maul had to kill Qui-Gon... Qui-Gon was the key to everything.»
- Battle of Naboo: «he knew that the battle was lost and that the boy would not die» (precognition). Damask tells the Commerce Guild, Techno Union and Corporate Alliance to begin a slow withdrawal from the Senate (CIS seed). Opponents are waylaid. Galaxies Opera, Treblanc: «The boy's actions already echo across the stars.»
- At the penthouse the Sun Guards have the night off. Sidious rehearses his speech; four bottles of Sullustan wine go down. Plagueis falls asleep for the first time in twenty years (L7207). Sidious leaves, stops, and the dark side whispers «Your election assured, the Sun Guards absent, Plagueis unsuspecting and asleep...». «And he moved in a blur.»
- Lightning grounds on the breathing device. «Plagueis's eyes snapped open, the Force gathering in him like a storm, but he stopped short of defending himself»; «Confident that he couldn't be killed... actually courting death». Sidious draws «more deeply on the dark side than he ever had». «You useless old fool.»
- Sidious's indictment speech: patricide; withheld secrets; «once choked him»; «allowed himself to be tricked by the Gran»; «egotistical quest for immortality»; «his equally powerful apprentice»; «Plagueis the Wise... who forged the most powerful Sith Lord the galaxy has ever known».
- Plagueis stands, collapses, and raises a FORCE STORM in concentric rings that «hurl objects to all corners». His «form became anamorphic».
- Sidious recites the Plagueis doctrine: «An apprentice no longer needs to be stronger... merely more clever... Strength is not in the flesh but in the Force.» «Teacher, yes... But Master-never.» He chokes him: «Try to keep yourself alive while I choke the life out of you.» «your own midi-chlorians can't accomplish what you're asking of them.»
- SIDIOUS CLAIMS HE COULD RESURRECT: «I could save you, of course. Return you from the brink, as you did Venamis. I could retask your body to repair...» (claims midi-chlorian mastery). «As we have clouded the minds of the Jedi, I clouded yours.» «The Sith'ari.» He claims Yinchorr, Dorvalla, Eriadu, Maul, the Neimoidians, Naboo, the clone army and Dooku were his ideas, «cleverly suggested to you». «I could have let you die in the Fobosi district... I acted wisely in rescuing you.» «I could not have succeeded without you.» «I will be proclaimed Emperor.»
- Plagueis dies face down; staged as a breathing-apparatus malfunction. 11-4D gets a new body. «a vague awareness of a power greater than himself. Was it Plagueis reaching out from the far side of death... Or... apotheosis?»
### Epilogue (L7305–7481)
- Plot: Palpatine elected. Damask's death goes barely noticed. At Theed Palpatine learns of Maul's defeat and explains his sense of loss; he wonders «how Maul had managed to kill a master sword fighter only to be overcome by a lesser one» (Qui-Gon > Obi-Wan as a swordsman, in Sidious's estimation). Qui-Gon's pyre; «ten thousand Jedi would follow Qui-Gon». «Palpatine was now the galaxy's sole Sith Lord.» Anakin «shown remarkable courage and Force ability» destroying the Droid Control Ship.
- Dooku at the LiMerge: «Your truer nature begins to reveal itself, I think.» Komari Vosa is alive and leading the Bando Gora. Sifo-Dyas «would be one step ahead of me». Dooku believes the Sith revealed himself deliberately as a declaration of war, and that Maul was the apprentice. «Eventually I will find him-or her»; «You wish to learn the secrets of the dark side?» «I confess that I do.» «Dooku was strong in the Force, and might simply be attempting to draw him out.»
- Obi-Wan («only recently been named a Jedi Knight») and Anakin visit. Palpatine sees «a touch of his younger self in Skywalker... The yet-unrecognized power.» «Dooku had talent, and could be a powerful placeholder.» «we will continue to follow your career with great interest.»
- FEATS Plagueis 32 BBY (death): Force storm while suffocating and under lightning (L7243); survives the first lightning barrage, possibly by choice (L7219); final visions (L7095, L7111).
- FEATS Sidious 32 BBY: blur-speed attack (L7217); lightning at his deepest draw (L7221); Force choke while Plagueis's midi-chlorians fail (L7251–7255); claimed ability to resurrect (L7259); clouded Plagueis's mind for 20+ years (L7267).
